demo-mode.purpose: allow UI testing without a Google account
behavior: load a built-in dataset of fake Gmail labels
make the demo mode selectable from the interface
keep preview and planning flows fully functional in demo mode
clearly indicate when the app is running without Google authentication

shared-behavior: apply the same operation ordering, source cleanup, progress tracking, and selection reset in demo and Google account modes
process the next operation only after the previous operation succeeds
refresh labels after each successful Google account operation
mode-parity.demo-mode: simulate label and mail-count updates locally
mode-parity.google-account-mode: execute Gmail API operations and use refreshed API values as the displayed source of truth
mode-parity.prohibited: never use the demo dataset or local demo mutation as the displayed result of a Google account operation

interface.layout: single unified tree with operation summary at top
components: operation-summary-top: displays sources, target, and operation count
label-hierarchy: single tree with 5 columns (Label, Mails, Source, Target, Actions)
source-selection: multiple checkboxes for selecting source labels
target-selection: single radio button for selecting target label
actions-column: inline rename and delete action buttons with icons
tree-toolbar: expand all and collapse all controls

tree-view: 5 columns: Label, Mails count, Source checkbox, Target radio, Actions
label icon displayed before each label name
expand/collapse controls for each node and global expand all / collapse all
delete action only enabled when mailCount is 0
dry-run: default preview mode before applying changes

gmail-api: merging moves messages to target label
log all operations without sensitive Gmail content
require explicit confirmation before modifying messages
paginate message listing and process message IDs with Gmail batchModify in batches of at most 1000
retry only transient API failures with bounded exponential backoff
verify merge, rename, and delete results through follow-up Gmail API reads
collision-handling: require manual resolution or a user-provided alternative name

performance: avoid loading all messages at once

unit: test collisions, empty labels, missing labels
integration: test UI with RTL or Playwright

safety: require explicit confirmation before modifying messages

goals: deliver a robust Gmail label management tool
maintain clean architecture and strict TypeScript typing
provide a minimalistic and efficient React UI
guarantee reliability through extensive automated testing
